Indicator 13 measures the proportion of newly diagnosed patients with atrial fibrillation who die within one year of diagnosis. This comparison evaluates performance across national, regional, and local hospital levels in [[danmark|Danmark]] [^src1]. 

Across all evaluated entities, no region or hospital met the required standard, with the "Standard opfyldt" (standard met) metric sitting at 0% for every single entry [^src1]. The national average for the current period is 13.1% [^src1]. Among the five regions, [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] recorded the highest mortality proportion at 14.1%, while [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] and [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] tied for the lowest at 12.6% [^src1]. [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] and [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] fell in between at 13.8% and 13.1%, respectively [^src1].

At the hospital level, [[kolding-sygehus|Kolding Sygehus]] is the clear outlier and leader in this unfortunate metric, recording the highest proportion among major units at 21.3% [^src1]. Næstved also shows a high rate of 20.0%, though this is based on a very small sample size of 4 out of 20 patients, resulting in a wide confidence interval [^src1]. Conversely, Sjællands Universitetshospital Roskilde reported the lowest proportion among standard hospital units at 8.8% [^src1]. Specialized or smaller clinics such as Garantiklinikken (3.6%) and Friklinikken Region Syddanmark Grindsted (2.2%) show lower percentages, while [[steno-diabetes-center|Steno Diabetes Center]] and Samsø Sundheds og Akuthus reported 0.0%, albeit with negligible patient counts [^src1]. Major university hospitals like [[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]] (15.9%) and OUH Odense Universitetshospital (14.1%) sit above the national average, whereas [[vejle-sygehus|Vejle Sygehus]] (10.4%) and Hospitalsenhed Midt (10.7%) perform better than the national baseline [^src1]. 

Because this data is drawn from a single reporting section, it does not support broad trend claims across multiple dated sections, though the table does include historical columns for 2020/21 and 2019/20 for context [^src1].
